difficultyReason: Short stimulus (38 words) with explicit 'therefore' marker immediately preceding the main conclusion. Correct answer directly paraphrases the concluding sentence. Distractors restate the premise about nutritional science.
stimulus: Nutritional science has recently shown that excessive sugar consumption increases the risk of heart disease. Therefore, governments should impose higher taxes on sugary beverages to discourage consumption and protect public health.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excessive sugar consumption has been shown to increase the risk of heart disease.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Governments should impose higher taxes on sugary beverages to discourage consumption and protect public health.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nutritional science is important for understanding dietary choices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sugary beverages are the primary cause of heart disease in developed nations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Public health protection requires eliminating all forms of sugar.

explanations.correct: The stimulus uses 'therefore' to signal that governments should impose higher taxes on sugary beverages. This is the main conclusion supported by the nutritional science claim.
explanations.A: This is a premise — the fact about nutritional science — not the conclusion the author is trying to establish.
explanations.C: Too vague and general; not what the argument concludes.
explanations.D: Overstates the claim. The stimulus says excessive sugar consumption increases risk, not that it is the primary cause.
explanations.E: Overstates the conclusion. The argument is about sugary beverages and taxation, not eliminating all sugar.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (42 words) with 'thus' immediately preceding the main conclusion. Correct answer paraphrases the concluding claim about artistic merit. Distractors restate supporting observations about artistic movements.
stimulus: The Impressionist movement revolutionized how artists approached light and color. Critics initially dismissed it as technically flawed, yet within decades it became central to art history. Thus, initial critical rejection does not determine an artwork's lasting artistic merit.
questionStem: The main point of the argument is that:

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Impressionist movement used innovative techniques with light and color.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Critics in the nineteenth century were often mistaken about new artistic movements.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Initial critical rejection does not determine an artwork's lasting artistic merit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Impressionism became important to art history within several decades.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All artworks that are initially rejected eventually become valued.

explanations.correct: The stimulus uses 'thus' to mark the main conclusion: initial rejection does not determine lasting merit. The Impressionist example supports this general claim.
explanations.A: This restates a supporting detail about the Impressionist movement, not the main conclusion.
explanations.B: A possible inference, but not the author's main point.
explanations.D: Another premise or supporting fact, not the conclusion.
explanations.E: Overstates the claim. The author only argues that initial rejection does not determine merit, not that all rejected work eventually becomes valued.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (36 words) with 'therefore' marking the main conclusion. Correct answer paraphrases the concluding statement about language learning. Distractors restate the age-related premise.
stimulus: Research shows that children acquire language most easily between ages two and four. Therefore, language instruction should be introduced early in childhood education programs.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children between ages two and four acquire language most easily.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Language instruction should be introduced early in childhood education programs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Research on language development is ongoing and important.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All children require the same language instruction methods.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Early childhood is the only time children can learn language effectively.

explanations.correct: 'Therefore' introduces the main conclusion: language instruction should be introduced early in childhood education. The research finding is the supporting premise.
explanations.A: This is the premise about language acquisition, not the conclusion.
explanations.C: Too general and vague; not the author's main point.
explanations.D: Not stated or implied by the argument.
explanations.E: Overstates the claim. The argument says early learning is easiest, not that it is the only time children can learn.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (40 words) with explicit 'hence' marker before the main conclusion. Correct answer paraphrases the policy recommendation. Distractors restate environmental premises.
stimulus: Plastic waste degrades very slowly and harms marine ecosystems. Single-use plastics account for the majority of ocean pollution. Hence, cities should implement comprehensive bans on single-use plastic products.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Plastic waste takes an extremely long time to degrade in natural environments.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Marine ecosystems suffer significant harm from plastic pollution.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cities should implement comprehensive bans on single-use plastic products.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single-use plastics are more harmful than other forms of pollution.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plastic pollution is the world's most serious environmental problem.

explanations.correct: 'Hence' signals the main conclusion: cities should implement bans on single-use plastics. The statements about degradation rates and marine harm are supporting premises.
explanations.A: A supporting premise about plastic degradation, not the main conclusion.
explanations.B: Another supporting fact about ecosystem harm, not the conclusion.
explanations.D: Not stated. The argument does not compare plastic to other forms of pollution.
explanations.E: Overstates the argument. The author argues for bans on single-use plastics, not that plastic is the world's most serious environmental problem.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (44 words) with 'so' introducing the main conclusion. Correct answer captures the ethical recommendation. Distractors restate supporting premises about corporate practices.
stimulus: Companies routinely collect personal data from online users without explicit consent. This data is sold to third parties for profit. So consumers deserve stronger legal protections against unauthorized data collection and sale.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Companies collect personal data from online users without explicit consent.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Personal data collected by companies is regularly sold to third parties for profit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Consumers deserve stronger legal protections against unauthorized data collection and sale.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Online privacy is less important than economic growth.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All companies should be prohibited from collecting any personal data.

explanations.correct: 'So' marks the main conclusion: consumers deserve stronger legal protections. The claims about data collection and sale are supporting premises for this policy recommendation.
explanations.A: A supporting premise describing current corporate practice.
explanations.B: Another supporting premise about what happens to collected data.
explanations.D: Not supported; the argument does not weigh privacy against economic growth.
explanations.E: Overstates the conclusion. The author argues for stronger protections, not a complete prohibition on data collection.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (39 words) with 'therefore' preceding the main conclusion. Correct answer paraphrases the economic claim. Distractors restate supporting information about interest rates.
stimulus: When interest rates rise, businesses delay expansion plans and consumer spending decreases. Therefore, central banks should consider the broader economic effects before raising interest rates.
questionStem: The main point of the argument is that:

choices.label: A

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consumer spending decreases as interest rates increase.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Central banks should consider the broader economic effects before raising interest rates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Interest rate increases are never justified in economic policy.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Consumer behavior is more important than business expansion.

explanations.correct: 'Therefore' introduces the main conclusion: central banks should consider broader effects before raising rates. The effects on business and consumer behavior are supporting premises.
explanations.A: A supporting premise about business response to interest rates.
explanations.B: Another supporting premise about consumer response.
explanations.D: Overstates the claim. The argument says central banks should consider effects, not that rate increases are never justified.
explanations.E: Not implied. The argument does not rank consumer behavior against business expansion.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (41 words) with 'thus' signaling the main conclusion. Correct answer paraphrases the medical recommendation. Distractors restate factual premises about medication effects.
stimulus: Antibiotic overuse promotes the development of drug-resistant bacteria. Patients often demand antibiotics for viral infections, where they are ineffective. Thus, doctors must resist patient pressure and prescribe antibiotics only when medically necessary.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibiotic overuse promotes the development of drug-resistant bacteria.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients frequently request antibiotics for conditions where they are ineffective.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doctors must resist patient pressure and prescribe antibiotics only when medically necessary.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Antibiotics are completely ineffective against viral infections.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All patient demands for medication should be denied.

explanations.correct: 'Thus' marks the main conclusion: doctors must resist pressure and prescribe only when medically necessary. The premises about overuse and patient behavior support this clinical recommendation.
explanations.A: A supporting premise about the dangers of overuse.
explanations.B: Another supporting premise about patient behavior.
explanations.D: Too strong. The argument says antibiotics are ineffective against viruses, not that they are completely ineffective in all contexts.
explanations.E: Overstates the conclusion. The argument is specifically about antibiotic prescribing, not all patient medication requests.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

choices.label: E
choices.text: All students learn best through the same instructional methods.

explanations.correct: 'Hence' marks the main conclusion: educators should incorporate diverse learning methods. The claims about retention and active learning are supporting premises for this pedagogical recommendation.
explanations.A: A supporting premise about retention and multiple formats.
explanations.B: Another supporting premise about active learning benefits.
explanations.D: Not stated. The argument does not single out lectures as least effective.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (40 words) with 'so' introducing the main conclusion. Correct answer captures the historical judgment. Distractors restate supporting details about technological development.
stimulus: The printing press dramatically increased the distribution of written materials across Europe. This technological innovation enabled wider literacy and facilitated the spread of new ideas. So the printing press was transformative to intellectual and social history.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The printing press increased the distribution of written materials across Europe.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Literacy rates improved following the invention of the printing press.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The printing press was transformative to intellectual and social history.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All technological innovations have significant social effects.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Written materials were rare before the invention of the printing press.

explanations.correct: 'So' marks the main conclusion: the printing press was transformative to history. The statements about distribution, literacy, and idea-spreading are supporting evidence for this historical judgment.
explanations.A: A supporting premise about the printing press's direct effect.
explanations.B: An inference from the supporting premises, but not the main conclusion.
explanations.D: Overgeneralizes. The argument is specifically about the printing press, not all technological innovations.
explanations.E: Not established by the argument. The stimulus does not address the rarity of written materials before printing.
